summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹987 mn and EBITDA margin reached 39%, with PAT up 87% YoY to ₹350 mn.
summary.overview: Ellenbarrie posted a strong Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations of ₹987 mn (+18% YoY, +13% QoQ), driven mainly by ramp-up of the Kurnool and Uluberia 2 plants. EBITDA rose to ₹387 mn (+21% YoY, +50% QoQ) at a 39% margin, which management attributed mainly to new power-efficient capacity, cost control and higher production rather than argon pricing. PAT of ₹350 mn was helped by lower finance cost and a lower effective tax rate. Management reaffirmed FY27 capex of ₹250 crore and FY28 capex of ₹200 crore, and said the East India 320 TPD on-site plant should start contributing revenue in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Core gases (bulk and on-site)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹973 mn, up 20% YoY, driven by merchant plant ramp-up; segment margin 38%, supported by volumes, cost efficiency and argon volumes and pricing.

segments.name: On-site vs bulk split (per Q1 investor presentation, as cited)
segments.commentary: On-site revenue about ₹14 crore and bulk about ₹70 crore, so on-site is about 20% of revenue, though on-site is a significantly higher share of capacity than 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance unchanged at ₹2,500 mn (₹250 crore); FY28 capex guidance ₹2,000 mn (₹200 crore).
East India 320 TPD on-site plant under commissioning; revenue expected from Q2 FY27.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 40% or higher as new capacity unfolds; management said this is a target, not a quarterly guarantee.
Merchant capacity in North India (220 TPD, not yet operational) and West Central India, together about 450–500 TPD, under construction; the West site is an ASU merchant plant.
Merchant plants assumed to take 18–24 months to ramp to 80–90% utilisation; payback described as about 18 months build plus 18–24 months ramp plus about three years.
risks_watch: Argon price volatility, which management said can move quarterly margins materially.
Ramp-up pace of Uluberia 2, Kurnool and the East India 320 TPD plant, and whether Q2 revenue from East India starts on time.
Power cost, which management called the largest cost; renewable PPA progress is key.
Competitive intensity in new merchant markets, where capacity is not pre-contracted and ramp takes 18–24 months.
Concentration in on-site contracts: one customer for the East India plant, and multiple large inquiries not yet signed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and margins, but cautious on argon pricing, which management repeatedly described as cyclical and not guaranteed to support quarterly margins. Answers on on-site customers and specific plant economics were guarded.
key_quotes: We expect this business to stabilize at 40% or higher EBITDA margins.
the growth in our EBITDA margins, however, has not been primarily on account of Argon pricing.
So, this entire 450, I mean, whatever residual amount that there is of this 450 crore will be towards these two merchant plants.
